title: Triangle Face Shape: Features & Styling Guide
summary: Learn how to identify a triangle face shape, tell it apart from heart and square faces, and explore hair, glasses, and makeup ideas.
body_markdown:
### Is a triangle face shape the same as a pear face shape?


Often, yes. Both terms commonly describe a face that is narrower at the forehead and wider at the jaw. Terminology varies, so compare the features rather than the label.


### What is the difference between triangle and inverted triangle face shapes?


They taper in opposite directions. A triangle face is wider at the jaw; an inverted triangle is wider across the upper face and narrows toward the chin.


### Does a wide jaw always mean I have a triangle face?


No. Compare the jaw with the forehead and cheekbones. If the forehead and jaw are similar in width, your outline may be closer to square; if the jaw is clearly widest and the forehead narrower, triangle is a better description.


### Can fuller cheeks make a face look triangular?


Fuller cheeks can affect how the face looks in photos, but cheek fullness alone does not define its shape. Check whether the jaw is wider than both the cheekbone area and the forehead, rather than judging from one feature.


### How can I get a clearer face-shape result from a photo?


Use a front-facing photo taken at eye level in even light. Keep your hair away from your forehead and jaw, and use a relaxed expression so the outer face is easy to see. You can then compare the outline yourself or try the[AI Face Analyzer](https://www.perfectcorp.com/business/showcase/face-analyzer) demo as a second point of reference.
